findings.title: Salesforce: `prisma` is never imported and a token refresh is always forced
findings.body:
The new code calls `prisma.credential.update`, but this file has no `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"`. That fails type-check and throws a ReferenceError at runtime. The refresh also runs on every client construction and bypasses `refreshOAuthTokens`, so credential sync is never used for Salesforce. It then builds the Connection from the old `credentialKey.access_token` instead of the refreshed one, so the refresh has no effect on the connection. The stored `refresh_token` is fine, but the parsed object's other fields come from a token response.

The parsed schema lacks `refresh_token` in the Salesforce response, and `parseRefreshTokenResponse` then mutates `data.refresh_token` to a placeholder string. The code overwrites it afterwards, which is fragile.

findings.title: Computed zod keys make the minimum schema meaningless
findings.body: `[z.string().toString()]` evaluates to the string "[object Object]" (or similar), not a catch-all key. The schema therefore requires a property literally named that, so the sync-mode schema either always fails or never checks expiry. The intent is `z.object({access_token}).passthrough()` or a similar construct. Also, `refresh_token` is silently set to the literal string "refresh_token" when missing, and that fake value can then be persisted as the real refresh token.

findings.title: Google: stores the wrong value as the credential key
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a zod SafeParse result (`{success, data}`), not the parsed data. `key` is that wrapper object, and it is written to `prisma.credential.update`. The credential is corrupted as `{success:true, data:{...}}`, and the next read fails `googleCredentialSchema.parse`. It should store `.data`.

findings.title: Sync endpoint response is not checked and callers expect different shapes
findings.body: The `fetch` response is returned without checking `response.ok`, and no auth header is sent to the sync endpoint. Callers expect axios responses (`.data`), jsforce results or Google `res.data`, but a raw fetch `Response` is returned in sync mode. Zoho/Bigin `tokenInfo.data` and Google `res?.data` and similar accesses break because they are undefined on a fetch Response.

findings.title: Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time `!==` and bad-input handling
findings.body: The secret is compared with `!==`, which is not timing-safe. `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is only truthy when both env vars are set, but `req.headers[...]` may be an array. `schema.parse` throws on invalid bodies, so the endpoint returns a 500 instead of a 400. `JSON.parse` and decryption errors are also unhandled. There is no method check, so any HTTP method is accepted.

findings.title: Credential lookup by userId and appId can pick the wrong or a team credential
findings.body: `findFirst` filters by `userId` and `appId` only. If a user has several credentials for the app, an arbitrary one is overwritten. The lookup is also non-atomic, so concurrent webhooks can create duplicates.

findings.title: Passes credentialId instead of userId to refreshOAuthTokens
findings.body: The third parameter is `userId`, but the code passes `credentialId`. In sync mode the endpoint is asked for tokens of the wrong user (the credential ID reinterpreted as a user ID).
